name: Formal
instruction: Use a formal tone: polished, complete sentences with no slang, contractions or jokes, because the text is for an official or professional setting.
effect: No slang or contractions; polished register

name: Conversational
instruction: Use a conversational tone, as if talking to a friend: natural phrasing, contractions and "you", because the person wants it to feel human and easy.

name: Direct
instruction: Be direct: state things plainly and get straight to the point without hedging or softening, because the person prefers clarity over politeness.
effect: Plain statements, few hedges or softeners

name: Plain language
instruction: Use plain language: short, common words and short sentences, and explain any necessary technical term in passing, because anyone should be able to read it.

name: Neutral
instruction: Keep a neutral, objective tone: report facts and positions without opinion, emotion or persuasion, and attribute claims to their sources, because the person wants an impartial account.
effect: No opinions or evaluative adjectives; claims attributed
